chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz Al-Abdi, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who circumambulated the House seven times as the obligatory circumambulation, then performed Sa'ee between As-Safa and Al-Marwa for four circuits, then his belly ached, so he went out and fulfilled his need, then he had intercourse with his wife. He (peace be upon him) said: He should perform Ghusl, then return and circumambulate three circuits, and seek forgiveness of his Lord, and there is nothing upon him.

I said: But if he had performed the obligatory circumambulation of the House, then circumambulated four circuits, then his belly ached, so he went out and fulfilled his need, then had intercourse with his wife? He said: His Hajj is spoiled, and upon him is a camel (as expiation), and he should perform Ghusl, then return and circumambulate seven circuits, then perform Sa'ee, and seek forgiveness of his Lord.

I said: Why did you not make it upon him, when he had intercourse with his wife before he finished his Sa'ee, just as you made upon him a sacrificial offering when he had intercourse with his wife before he finished his circumambulation? He said: Indeed, the circumambulation is obligatory, and therein is prayer, and the Sa'ee is a Sunnah from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

I said: Is it not that Allah says, 'Surely As-Safa and Al-Marwa are among the rituals of Allah'? He said: Yes, but He has said regarding them, 'And whoever does good voluntarily, then surely Allah is Grateful, Knowing'. So, if the Sa'ee were obligatory, He would not have said, 'And whoever does good voluntarily'.

key_terms.سَعْيٌ: Sa'ee (ritual walking between Safa and Marwa)
key_terms.غَمَزَهُ بَطْنُهُ: His belly ached (urgency to relieve himself)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in Hajj rulings if a man has intercourse with his wife before or after completing the obligatory circumambulation (Tawaf)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia juristic distinction between obligatory (fard) and sunnah acts within Hajj, specifically contrasting the status of Tawaf al-Ifadah with Sa'ee. Imam al-Sadiq (as) argues that since Sa'ee is classified as a Sunnah based on the Quranic phrase 'whoever volunteers good,' its interruption does not invalidate the core ritual like the obligatory Tawaf does. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on textual interpretation of Quranic grammar to determine ritual hierarchy and expiation requirements.

en.hubeali: Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz Al Abdy, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who circumambulated by the House (Kabah) seven Obligatory circumambulations. Then he performed Sa’ee between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, four circuits. Then his belly ached, so he went out and fulfilled his need. Then he overwhelmed his wife. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should wash, then return, so he should circumambulate three (remaining) circuits, and he should seek Forgiveness of his Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, and there is nothing upon him’.

I said, ‘Supposing it was circumambulation of the House (Kabah), the Obligatory circumambulation, so he circumambulated four circuits, then his belly ached, so he went out and fulfilled his need, and overwhelmed his wife?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘His Hajj would be spoilt, and upon him would be a sacrificial animal, and he should wash, then return, so he should circumambulate seven (circuits), then perform Sa’ee, and he should seek Forgiveness of his Lord<sup>azwj</sup>’.

I said, ‘How come you<sup>asws</sup> did not make to be upon him, where he overwhelmed his wife before he was free from his Sa’ee, just as you<sup>asws</sup> are making it to be upon him, a sacrificial offering where he overwhelms his wife before he is free from his circumambulation?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The circumambulation is Obligatory, and therein is Prayer, and the Sa’ee, being a Sunnah from Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’.

I said, ‘Isn’t Allahazwj Saying that [2:158] Surely the Safa and the Marwa are among the Rituals appointed by Allah?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, but Heazwj has Said [2:158] and whoever does good voluntarily, then surely Allah is Grateful, Knowing. So, had the Sa’ee been Obligatory, Heazwj would not have Said [2:158] and whoever does good voluntarily’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ibn Mahbub has narrated from ‘Abd al-‘Aziz al-‘Abdiy from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who performs seven time Tawaf around the House, then performs Sa‘y between al-Safa’ and al-Marwah four times, and feels trouble in his stomach. He then goes to his lodging and relieves himself; then he overwhelms his wife for (sexual intercourse). He (the Imam) said, ‘He must do Ghusl (bath) and return to complete his Sa‘y between al-Safa’ and al-Marwah with another three walking, ask his Lord for forgiveness and there is nothing on him.’

I then asked, ‘What is the rule if he performs obligatory Tawaf around the House, and after the fourth round of walking he feels trouble in his stomach, goes to relieve himself and overwhelms his wife for (sexual intercourse). He (the Imam) said, ‘His al-Hajj is destroyed, he owes one badanah. He must do Ghusl (bath), go back to perform Tawaf of seven times, then perform Sa‘y between al- Safa’ and al-Marwah and ask his Lord for forgiveness.’

I asked, ‘Why is there not anything on him when he performs sexual intercourse with his wife before completing Sa‘y of seven times walking for complete Sa‘y, as he owes one offering because of his sexual intercourse with his wife before completing Tawaf? He (the Imam) said, ‘Tawaf is obligatory and there is Salat (prayer) with it. Sa‘y is of the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause.

I then said, ‘Has Allah not said, “Al-Safa’ and al-Marwah are of the reminders of Allah?”’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, He has done so, there are also these words of Allah (to consider), “If one volunteers goodness he will find Allah appreciative and all-Knowing.” Had Sa‘y been obligatory He would not say, “Those who volunteer”.”’
